subject.title: iOS app: push notifications for assistant messages + background Talk mode

question: Should native iOS assistant-message notifications ship as generic APNs alerts by default, expose transcript previews only behind explicit opt-in, or remain unsupported until a broader mobile notification privacy model is approved?
rationale: The APNs relay, registration, local notification, and exec-approval pieces exist, but payload content, lock-screen privacy, tap routing, duplicate foreground behavior, and per-node opt-in semantics require maintainer product and security intent before implementation.

options.title: Generic Alerts First
options.body: Add a dedicated chat-reply APNs kind with generic notification text by default, tap routing to the correct chat, and leave transcript previews for a later explicit opt-in.

options.title: Opt-In Previews
options.body: Allow assistant reply text in APNs only behind a visible per-device or per-gateway privacy setting with docs and live lock-screen proof.

options.title: Defer Native Chat Push
options.body: Keep relying on foreground app state and third-party channels until maintainers define a broader mobile notification policy.

recommendation.title: Generic Alerts First
recommendation.body: Add a dedicated chat-reply APNs kind with generic notification text by default, tap routing to the correct chat, and leave transcript previews for a later explicit opt-in.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the APNs relay and exec-approval notification flows that the native chat notification contract would extend.
